'''Steven Dillingham''' (born May 12, 1952) is an American lawyer who served as the 25th [[Director of the United States Census Bureau|director]] of the [[United States Census Bureau]] from January 7, 2019, to January 20, 2021.

==Education==
Dillingham graduated from [[Rock Hill High School (South Carolina)|Rock Hill High School]] in [[Rock Hill, South Carolina]], in 1970. From 1970 to 1972 he attended the [[United States Air Force Academy|US Air Force Academy]]. Dillingham graduated from [[Winthrop University]] in 1973 with a bachelor's degree in political science. He received his [[Juris Doctor|J.D.]], [[Master of Public Administration|M.P.A.]], and [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[University of South Carolina]], and completed his [[Master of Business Administration|M.B.A.]] at the [[George Washington University School of Business]] and [[Master of Laws|LL.M.]] at [[Georgetown University Law Center|Georgetown Law]].<ref name=":2" />

== Career ==
Dillingham is a career member of the U.S. federal government's [[Senior Executive Service (United States)|Senior Executive Service]], with more than 25 years of statistical, research, senior management, and legal experience. Dillingham's prior experience heading federal statistical service agencies includes a stint as Director of the [[Bureau of Justice Statistics]] and the [[Bureau of Transportation Statistics]]. Dillingham also served as Director of the [[Peace Corps]] Office of Strategic Information, Research, and Planning. Other federal service includes directing research and planning for the [[United States Department of Justice|Department of Justice]]'s [[United States Trustee Program]], and directing surveys for the [[Office of Personnel Management]].<ref name=":2" />

In addition, Dillingham was the deputy director for the National District Attorneys Association and administrator of the American Prosecutors Research Institute. Dillingham has served on the faculties of the [[University of South Carolina]] and [[George Mason University]]. He is a senior certified professional with the [[Society for Human Resource Management]].<ref name=":2" />

=== U.S. Census ===
Dillingham was sworn in as the 25th [[Director of the United States Census Bureau|director]] of the [[United States Census Bureau]] on January 7, 2019.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.census.gov/newsroom/bios/execs/dillingham-steven.html|title=Dr. Steven Dillingham|publisher=United States Census Bureau|website=www.census.gov|language=EN-US|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref> He was nominated by President [[Donald Trump]] in 2018 and was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] in a unanimous vote on January 2, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Winthrop Alumnus Confirmed as Census Bureau Director|url=https://www.winthrop.edu/news-events/winthrop-alumnus-confirmed-as-census-bureau-director.aspx|access-date=2020-08-08|website=www.winthrop.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Steven Dillingham Confirmed as Director of the Census|url=https://www.amstat.org/asa/News/Steven-Dillingham-Confirmed-as-Director-of-the-Census.aspx#:~:text=The%20Senate%20confirmed%20Steven%20Dillingham,preparations%20for%20the%20upcoming%20census.|access-date=2020-08-08|website=www.amstat.org}}</ref>  On January 18, 2021, Dillingham announced his retirement effective January 20, 2021;<ref name="census_dillingham-farewell">{{cite web |last1=Dr. Steven Dillingham, Director - United States Census Bureau. |title=Director's Blog: Farewell (archived). |url=https://www.census.gov/newsroom/blogs/director/2021/01/dillingham-farewell.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210119004417/https://www.census.gov/newsroom/blogs/director/2021/01/dillingham-farewell.html |access-date=January 18, 2021|archive-date=January 19, 2021 }}</ref> his appointment was set to last until the end of 2021.<ref name=WPost>{{cite web |last=Bahrampour |first=Tara |title=Embattled Census Bureau Director Steven Dillingham resigns |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/social-issues/embattled-census-bureau-director-steven-dillingham-resigns/2021/01/18/63c8d1aa-59bb-11eb-a976-bad6431e03e2_story.html |date=January 21, 2021 |newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref> His departure from the office was marked by accusations that he supported a partisan effort to try to use potentially inaccurate data on undocumented immigrants to exclude them from congressional apportionment.<ref name=WPost/><ref>{{cite web |last=Konrad |first=Nicholas |title=How the Census Bureau Stood Up to Donald Trump's Meddling |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/08/12/sunday-review/census-redistricting-trump-immigrants.html |date=August 12, 2021 |newspaper=The New York Times}}</ref>
